title: Fringe Show 10: Come Dine With Me ⭐️⭐️ @Edinburgh Festival Fringe @Un...
transcript: One of the recent trends in musical theater adaptations has been reality TV shows turned into musicals. And following the footsteps of the absolutely charming great British Bake Off musical, comes the newest musical, Come Dine With Me, which is based off the reality TV show of the same name, where contestants will cook dinner for each other and rank their dinners. And one of the unique aspects of this musical that I really appreciated was that it chose to focus primarily on the people behind the scenes that are filming the show. Like, the main characters are the camera guy, the sound guy, and, like, the director, rather than focusing on the individual contestants who are also characters and also play a big part in this show. Actually, that's where the positive aspects of this musical for me ended. I really did not enjoy this one. I never really got invested in any of the characters or any of the tension that was happening. A part of this musical is that somebody is sabotaging the other dinners, and it's unclear if that's a bad thing or if it's going to make good television. You weren't really sure what side to be on or who to root for. The musical numbers were all incredibly generic, and none of them felt like they were necessary to this story, which is unfortunate, because I think that when you're doing a reality TV show musical, there's very easy musical numbers in there. In Terms of, like, highlighting each of the contestants and getting to see each of their point of views. And this show kind of tried to do that, but you didn't care about any of the characters. And I think part of that was because, again, the contestants were not the main characters of the show, which I think can work, but just didn't in this adaptation. I definitely think there are aspects of the concept of this musical that could be expanded and make for interesting material, but input all together, this musical just ended up being rather confusing and rather lackluster. There were definitely performances in this that I really enjoyed, specifically like Harry Chandler as the lead sound guy. But the character development throughout the show just wasn't enough to latch on to. Come dine with me is currently playing at Underbelly Bristol Square through the end of the fringe.
classificationReason: First-hand review of an Edinburgh Fringe musical with clear personal opinions ('I really did not enjoy this one', 'never really got invested'). Not on the provided show list.
